extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH grant applications (Multiple PI and single-project R01/R21) who must submit a Leadership Plan (PHS 398 Section I).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and example language for preparing Leadership Plans required in NIH Multiple-PI grant applications (and examples for single-project leadership plans such as R01/R21), covering roles, decision-making, IP, conflict resolution, and administrative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership Plan inclusion and location
rubrics_metrics.description: For Multiple PI applications, a new section for Leadership Plans (PHS 398, Section I) must be included, unless the RFA announcement requests the information be provided in another section. There are no page limitations for Section I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a Leadership Plan in PHS 398 Section I for Multiple-PI applications unless the funding announcement directs otherwise. Section I has no page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles/areas of responsibility of the PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify roles/areas of responsibility of the PIs (e.g., oversight of the Program, implementation of the Scientific Agenda, responsibility for particular specific aims, approvals for animal/human research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete assignments: which PI oversees which aims, who is responsible for animal research approvals, who supervises which staff. Example language: 'PI#1 will oversee aim 1 and be responsible for all animal research approvals.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal and management coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe fiscal and management coordination among PIs, including which PI serves as contact PI for fiscal/administrative management or whether each PI is responsible for their own fiscal administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: contact PI assumes fiscal and administrative management and maintains communication; or 'Each PI will be responsible for his own fiscal and research administration.' Clarify who submits reports and handles institutional financial matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for making decisions on scientific direction and allocation of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how decisions about scientific direction and allocation/reprogramming of funds will be made (e.g., PIs meet to discuss changes, Steering Committee oversight, authority to reallocate funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide decision-making processes and delegation of authority: e.g., 'The Steering Committee will oversee decisions on minor changes in research direction and have the authority to reallocate funds and resources between PIs.' Include how major vs minor decisions are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing and communication among investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe mechanisms for data sharing and communication among investigators (sharing research results, frequency and modes of communication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: weekly communications by phone/e-mail/in person; monthly meetings; 'All PIs will share their respective research results with other PIs, key personnel, and consultants.' Specify routine practices to discuss experimental design and data analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide publication policy and authorship criteria (e.g., authorship based on the relative scientific contributions of the PIs and key personnel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how authorship will be determined and any agreed publication procedures. Example: 'Publication authorship will be based on the relative scientific contributions of the PIs and key personnel.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property (IP) policies and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe intellectual property policies, including negotiation of agreements, formation of an IP committee, access rights for project purposes, and treatment of pre-existing IP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Technology Transfer Offices prepare and negotiate agreements; 'An Intellectual Property Committee composed of representatives from each institution ... will be formed'; PIs may grant necessary access rights on a non-exclusive royalty-free basis for the project; rights in pre-existing IP remain with the creating party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for resolving conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe procedures for resolving conflicts among PIs (e.g., initial PI meeting to resolve dispute, then arbitration committee or escalation to departmental administrators/senior executives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include escalation steps and composition of adjudicating bodies: e.g., refer to an arbitration committee consisting of impartial senior executives from each PI's institution and a mutually agreed third; members should not be directly involved in the research or dispute. Example includes a 30-business-day window for departmental administrators to attempt resolution before escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact PI responsibilities and NIH communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the contact PI and specify responsibilities such as serving as contact for NIH, assuming fiscal and administrative management, maintaining communication among PIs and key personnel, and submitting annual progress reports and necessary documents (e.g., IRB approvals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify who will submit progress reports and communicate with NIH. Example: 'PI#1 will serve as contact PI and will assume fiscal and administrative management ... He will be responsible for communication with NIH and submission of annual reports.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotation of leadership roles
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, describe rotation of contact/Chair roles among PIs (e.g., contact PI rotated to PI#2 in even years; Chair rotates yearly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State period/frequency of rotation and how responsibilities are transitioned. Example: 'The responsibilities of the contact PI will be rotated to PI #2 in even years of the grant award.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Steering Committee structure and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Steering Committee will be used, describe its membership (PIs, key personnel, consultants), and duties such as oversight and coordination of project management, research administration, publications, data sharing, and integration of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out the committee's authority (e.g., oversight of minor changes, reallocation of funds), who chairs it, meeting schedules and agenda responsibilities, and how membership is chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in PI location and replacement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide procedures if a PI moves institutions or cannot carry out duties, including attempts to transfer the relevant portion of the grant and processes for recruiting and approving a replacement PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provisions: attempt to transfer the portion of the grant to new institution; recruit a replacement at a participating institution; replacement may be subject to Steering Committee and Institution approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with laws, DHHS and NIH policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe responsibilities to ensure institutional compliance with US laws, DHHS and NIH policies including biosafety, human and animal research, and data and facilities management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language: '... ensure that systems are in place to guarantee institutional compliance with US laws, DHHS and NIH policies including biosafety, human and animal research, data and facilities.' Identify which PI(s) will ensure compliance and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of supervision and effort for key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify supervision responsibilities and effort allocation for key personnel (e.g., which PI supervises specific technicians or postdocs and the percent effort devoted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete supervisory assignments and effort levels: e.g., 'She will supervise the Technician #2 at 50% effort for the flow cytometry studies and the post Doc for the endothelial cell studies.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication frequency, scheduling and agendas
rubrics_metrics.description: State frequency of routine communications (e.g., weekly or monthly), communication modes (phone, e-mail, in person), and responsibilities for meeting schedules and agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in text: weekly communications to discuss experimental design, data analysis; monthly meetings to maintain communication among PIs and key personnel; Chair responsible for meeting schedules and agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget subdivision and individual PI budget responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how award funds will be subdivided and which PI(s) are responsible for their respective budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The Institution will subdivide the award funds and each PI will be responsible for his own budget.' Clarify processes for reprogramming or reallocating funds when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property committee composition and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: If used, describe the composition of the Intellectual Property Committee (representatives from each institution) and its duties to ensure IP developed by the PIs is protected according to the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'An Intellectual Property Committee composed of representatives from each institution that is part of the grant award, will be formed to work together to ensure the intellectually property developed by the PIs is protected according to the policies established in the agreement.' Also note Technology Transfer Offices' role.
